headline_marked: 7th title for Australia: [[Australia wins Women's T20 World Cup]] beating England
headline: 7th title for Australia: Australia wins Women's T20 World Cup beating England
summary: Australia dominated the final at Lord's, defeating the hosts England by 7 wickets to secure their seventh championship trophy.
details: Australia's women's team has further solidified their dominance in the T20 World Cup by defeating England by 7 wickets in the final at Lord's.
This victory marks Australia's seventh title in the tournament's history. Notably, no other team has managed to win two trophies in the competition.
England batted first and scored 150 runs for the loss of 4 wickets in 20 overs. Captain Nat Sciver-Brunt scored an unbeaten 58 and Freya Kemp remained not out on 44.
In response, Australia reached the target with 17 balls to spare, losing only 3 wickets. A century partnership of 117 runs between Beth Mooney and Phoebe Litchfield was key to the victory.
Beth Mooney scored 64 runs off 49 balls, while Phoebe Litchfield contributed 48 runs off 35 balls. Beth Mooney was named Player of the Final and Player of the Tournament.
England's total of 150 was not enough to stop the Australian side, who secured the win nearly three overs before the end of the innings.
caption:
7 titles and counting! Australia continues to dominate the Women's T20 World Cup.

Australia's women's team has further solidified their dominance in the T20 World Cup by defeating England by 7 wickets in the final at Lord's.

This victory marks Australia's seventh title in the tournament's history. Notably, no other team has managed to win two trophies in the competition.

England batted first and scored 150 runs for the loss of 4 wickets in 20 overs. Captain Nat Sciver-Brunt scored an unbeaten 58 and Freya Kemp remained not out on 44.

In response, Australia reached the target with 17 balls to spare, losing only 3 wickets. A century partnership of 117 runs between Beth Mooney and Phoebe Litchfield was key to the victory.

Beth Mooney scored 64 runs off 49 balls, while Phoebe Litchfield contributed 48 runs off 35 balls. Beth Mooney was named Player of the Final and Player of the Tournament.

England's total of 150 was not enough to stop the Australian side, who secured the win nearly three overs before the end of the innings.

Source: Prothom Alo, Somoy News
